text:
Jordan (Product): quick follow-up from today's pricing Q&A — capturing sticky items here. Main user concern: sudden traffic bursts during marketing launches and how that interacts with per-minute and monthly credits.

Kai (Finance): TL;DR: tokens are consumed as usual. We enforce per-route and per-org windows. We have a configurable grace-burst for paid tiers (enterprise: 30s, standard: 15s). Beyond that you get 429s or soft-rejects depending on policy. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Rina (Billing Ops): note on credits: standard promo credits expire after 12 months; trial credits 90 days. We also have an "auto-topup" flag for orgs that want pre-authorized purchases when they hit a threshold. Topups are optional and off by default.

Noah (Support): headers you'll see on throttles: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-Quota-Window` (seconds), `Retry-After`. We're testing `X-Credit-Balance` for customers who opt in. Body includes `{"error":"rate_limited","retry_after_seconds":60}`.

Jordan (Product): customers asked about more nuanced signals so they can client-side smooth. Is there a roadmap item for richer feedback?

taylor_s (eng): yes — roadmap includes "token smoothing" and "quota shadow mode" (early access). Token smoothing spreads request bursts across a short window to avoid hard 429s for spiky workloads. Quota shadow mode lets customers preview quota enforcement without blocking for 14 days.

Rina (Billing Ops): for Dedicated: reserved capacity doesn't draw hosted credits. If you opt into cross-fallback (opt-in setting), hosted units are consumed only when Dedicated falls back to hosted during outages. We show both balances in the billing console: "Reserved usage" and "Hosted credits".

Kai (Finance): demo/launch capacity — we provide short demo passes: 72-hour auto-approve up to 3x baseline for partners, 48-hour 2x for standard paid plans. Above that requires Sales sign-off. Submit via Support with anticipated peak TPS + token/sec.

Noah (Support): refund/adjustment policy: if misconfiguration or platform error consumed credits, we audit and typically issue adjustments in 3-7 business days. Requests must include request ids and timestamps.

Jordan (Product): any new API endpoints for programmatic balance checks?

Rina (Billing Ops): yes: `GET /v1/account/credits` (lightly rate-limited) and `GET /v1/usage/summary` (per-route breakdown). Example: `{"balance":"12000","expires_at":"2027-01-15T00:00:00Z","pending_topup":"false"}` (that payload is returned as JSON string in body).

taylor_s (eng): ops detail: when we throttle we try these steps in order: 1) apply smoothing, 2) attempt model-variant fallback (lower-precision quantized), 3) route to a slower ready pool, 4) return 429. Customers can control fallbacks via policy: `fallback: [quantized-v2,small-gpu-pool]`.

Ava (CEO): quick strategic note: no major pricing changes planned next quarter. We're focusing on clearer guidance for model-family pricing and quantization discounts. Expect docs + examples next month.

Jordan (Product): follow-ups I'll own: 1) draft FAQ with header examples and error bodies, 2) sample client backoff recipe (exponential + jitter + respect Retry-After), 3) support doc for demo pass flow. Will post by EOD.

OpsBot: Transcript and slides uploaded: https://redwood.internal/s/all-hands/2026-03-22-pricing

Kai (Finance): last operational note — orgs using Hosted + Dedicated under the same billing account: Dedicated gets charged via reserved billing first; hosted credits cover any fallthrough. We plan to show an "effective credit burn" metric to make charges clearer.

Noah (Support): I'll prepare customer-facing wording and examples for the Support KB, tagging @Jordan for review.

Jordan (Product): thanks everyone. If any partners need an early preview of quota shadow mode, DM me and we'll add you to the EA list. :thumbsup:
